input: Investigate peer-to-peer lending platforms this week

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: P2P lending can be investigated from many angles — as a borrower, an investor, a competitor, or an academic researcher. Knowing what specifically to cover (fees, returns, risks, platform comparisons) shapes the entire research agenda.
Whether this is personal research, for a business, for a client, or for a team determines the depth, format, and who the findings need to satisfy.
The relevant platforms, regulations, and currency of information vary significantly by country or region, so geography is a critical filter.
The user said 'this week,' but knowing how many hours they can realistically dedicate shapes how deep the investigation can go.
Without knowing the intended outcome — a decision to invest, a written report, a shortlist of platforms — it's impossible to know when the investigation is 'done well.'
The user may want to focus on high-yield/high-risk platforms vs. safer established ones, or prefer consumer lending vs. business lending — this priority filter narrows which platforms to examine.
Knowing whether the user wants to capture findings in a comparison spreadsheet, a written summary, a note-taking app, or just a mental decision determines the format of the work itself.

gold.taskTitle: Investigate peer-to-peer lending platforms this week
gold.taskDescription: Research peer-to-peer lending platforms within the week to reach an informed understanding or decision about them.

questions.title: What is the main reason you are investigating these platforms?
questions.description: Understand whether the user intends to invest money, borrow money, conduct competitive analysis, or something else entirely — this is the single biggest scope-setter.

questions.title: Who will use the findings from this investigation?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is purely personal, for a team, a client, or a business decision, which affects required depth and presentation.

questions.title: Which country or region should the platforms be based in?
questions.description: P2P lending platforms, regulations, and available options differ enormously by geography, so this filters the entire research scope.

questions.title: How many hours this week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Knowing the available time budget determines how many platforms can be reviewed and how deep each analysis can go.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like at the end of the week?
questions.description: Establish the concrete deliverable or decision the user expects — e.g., a shortlist of 3 platforms, a go/no-go investment decision, or a written comparison.

questions.title: Do you prioritise higher returns, lower risk, or a specific loan type?
questions.description: Understanding the user's risk/return preference and whether they care about consumer, real-estate, or business loans helps filter which platforms are worth investigating.

questions.title: Where do you want to record and organise your findings?
questions.description: Knowing the preferred tool — spreadsheet, notes app, document, or no formal record — shapes how the research tasks are structured and handed off.
